blocks.text: INNNEWS - Soekarno ideology built in context of 20th century colonialism. Nationalism in those days served as a liberating energy and a consolidating tool of a new free nation. But eighty years later, the structure of global power has been significantly altered. International relations are no longer simply defined by territorial occupation, but by economic networks, military alliances, information technology, and ideological influences across borders.
In that context, nationalism cannot be maintained as historical rhetoric alone. It has to be redefined to read global dynamics rationally and consistently.

Response to international conflict shows a double standard in nationalism. When the Russians attacked Ukraine, some of them allowed that action with an argument that Ukraine was in NATO orbit. The developing narrative puts the West as a main trigger of escalation.

Instead, when the United States and Israel are directly conflicted with Iran, a harsh crackdown is immediately mobilized in the name of national sovereignty. But public debate often ignores the fact that Iran also builds strategic proxy and influence networks in different Middle East countries. In some cases, the effects of military escalation are felt by other Muslim countries who are not directly involved.
This phenomenon shows that nationalism is often practiced selectively. It becomes an emotional identity determined by geopolitics preferences, not by consistent ethics principles.
Therefore, the basic question is: what is colonization in contemporary politics?

If in the 20th century colonization was identical to physical occupation by foreign forces, in the 21st century the shape was much more complex. Economic penetration, technology domination, information control, political intervention through a proxy network, so that the manipulation of local elite can be an effective power instrument without having to raise a flag in a controlled area.

Furthermore, colonization doesn't always come from the outside. When a regime limits civil liberties, silences criticism, hogging public narratives, and sacrificing people's well-being for the ambition of power, there are internal dominance forms that are substantially no different from classical colonialism. In this situation, nationalism that refuses criticism in the name of sovereignty is at risk of misleading injustice.

A healthy nationalism has to be rooted in moral consistency. It's not a side of a particular block, but it's a side of principle. It places the sovereignty of the people as a core, rather than maintaining regime legitimacy. He also dared to criticize the violation of sovereignty and humanity, carried out by foreign forces and domestic elite.

Young-thinkers have a responsibility to formulate the new paradigm of Indonesian nationalism. The paradigm needs to be based on universal ethics, mature geopolitics, and intellectual courage to judge objective conflicts. Without conceptual renewal, nationalism is potentially reduced to a propaganda instrument. At that point, the colonized was no longer territorial territory, but the collective consciousness of the nation itself.
